result.topic_en: Euler begins his clarifications on the theory of variations for functions of one variable, stating the general problem: how much an integral formula ∫Z dx changes when the function y is replaced by an infinitely close one, and then starts to recast it geometrically with a curve AM over axis AP.
result.transcription:

caſus nonnulli particulares omni ſtudio et diligentia fuerint euoluti, quin etiam ipſa pars prior, quae tantum circa functiones vnius variabilis verſatur neutiquam adhuc ſatis clare et diſtincte eſt enucleata, ita vt perſpicue intelligeremus veram indolem atque naturam ſingularum partium, quibus variationem contineri inuenimus, quem in finem dilucidationes ſequentes hic adiungere viſum eſt.

Dilucidationes ſuper Theoria variationum ad functiones ſaltem vnius variabilis accommodata.

31. Quaeſtiones quae hic occurrunt ad hoc problema generale reuocare licet:

Explicatio ipſius Problematis.

Si $y$ fuerit functio quaecunque ipſius $x$, indeque definiatur valor cuiuspiam formulae integralis datae $\int Z\,dx$, denotante $Z$ expreſſionem ex ipſis quantitatibus $x$ et $y$ earumque differentialium rationibus vtcunque compoſitam, quaeſtio eſt, ſi loco illius functionis $y$ alia quaecunque illi proxima ſeu infinite parum tantum ab ea diſcrepans adhibeatur, quanto maiorem minoremve valorem, tum eadem formula integralis $\int Z\,dx$ ſit conſecutura.

items.quote: Si $y$ fuerit functio quaecunque ipſius $x$, indeque definiatur valor cuiuspiam formulae integralis datae $\int Z\,dx$, denotante $Z$ expreſſionem ex ipſis quantitatibus $x$ et $y$ earumque differentialium rationibus vtcunque compoſitam, quaeſtio eſt, ſi loco illius functionis $y$ alia quaecunque illi proxima ſeu infinite parum tantum ab ea diſcrepans adhibeatur, quanto maiorem minoremve valorem, tum eadem formula integralis $\int Z\,dx$ ſit conſecutura.
items.english: If y is any function of x, and from it the value of some given integral formula ∫Z dx is determined, where Z denotes an expression composed in any way of the quantities x and y and the ratios of their differentials, the question is: if in place of that function y some other function next to it, i.e. differing from it only infinitely little, is used, by how much greater or smaller a value the same integral formula ∫Z dx will then attain.

items.quote: quem in finem dilucidationes ſequentes hic adiungere viſum eſt.
items.english: to which end it seemed good to add the following clarifications here.

items.quote: eam more ſoluito ad Geometriam reuocemus.
items.english: let us, in the usual manner, bring it back to geometry.
